references.title: Early supplementation of enteral microlipid and fish oil in premature infants with enterostomy: the EMLFO trial

characteristics.name: Methods
characteristics.value:
Study design: Open-labeled Randomized control trial

Country: USA

Setting: NICU at Brenner Children's Hospital, Wake Forest Baptist Medical Center

Study dates: Unclear; Study protocol published in 2011, results published in 2014

characteristics.name: Participants
characteristics.value:
Total number: 37

Inclusion criteria: Premature infants <2 months of age with jejunostomy or ileostomy

Exclusion criteria: Infants with colostomy, congenital anomaly, metabolic disease, received feeds for > 4 days or unable to initiate enteral feeds for > 28 days after ostomy placement

characteristics.name: Interventions
characteristics.value:
Control group description: Usual care without fish oil or enteral fat

Intervention group's description: 2 g/day of Fish oil (Major fish oil 500, Major Pharmaceuticals, Livonia, Michigan; Rugby Sea Omega 50, Rugby Pharmaceuticals Inc., Corona, California) and Microlipid (safflower oil; Nestle Nutrition, Florham Park, New Jersey)

characteristics.name: Outcomes
characteristics.value:
Primary outcomes: Nutritional outcomes, growth

Secondary outcomes: Conjugated bilirubin, sepsis, antibiotic use, duration of central venous catheter use, central line-associated bloodstream infection, duration of parenteral nutrition, intravenous lipid emulsion requirement, mortality

characteristics.name: Notes
characteristics.value:
Funding source: Intramural funds and Gerber Foundation Fund

Declarations of interest :None

Contact with authors: None

risk-of-bias.support-for-judgement: Block randomization, with a block of 8.
Sealed envelopes were used to conceal the randomization assessments, it is not clear if other measures were taken to ensure concealment such as opaque envelopes.
37 infants were randomized, but data is provided for only 36 infants.
The outcomes to be studied are not well described in the methodology.
